title: R_3(5(x-y)=4z) = 141
statement: The 3-colour Rado number of the equation 5(x-y) = 4z is exactly 141: every 3-colouring of {1,...,141} contains a monochromatic solution, and some 3-colouring of {1,...,140} avoids one.

concept_refs.note: authored this session at math-education graph/concepts/rado-number.md (uncommitted); flip to resolved with a fresh graph_pin once that repo commits
Rado numbers are the arithmetic-Ramsey analogue: the same threshold/colouring reasoning at a different structure

provenance.conjectured_by: literature: Y. Chang, J. A. De Loera, W. J. Wesley, 'Rado Numbers and SAT Computations', ISSAC 2022 / arXiv:2210.03262

evidence.notes: RE-CERTIFIED 2026-08-12 inside axeyum's own stack: the proof was produced by the in-tree proof-producing CDCL core streaming TEXT DRAT to disk (0.002 s, 267 steps), read back through axeyum's own parse_drat, and re-derived by axeyum's own backward DRAT checker (0.003 s). No external solver and no external checker took part. SUPERSEDES the original kissat certificate (sha256 6e3d050b819d5e5324c482ee14be7ffc61cf840a2d7a9e678887d877ee1574bb, 12240 bytes), which was BINARY DRAT: drat-trim verified it, but axeyum's own parse_drat reads text DRAT, so the shipped system could not read the certificate it shipped (findings register B8). The deciding CNF beside it regenerates byte-identically from the claim's parameters.
